capabilities: sync the vault across devices through the user's own Dropbox, OneDrive, or Google Drive account
encrypt file contents end-to-end (AES-256-GCM) or protect plugin settings files
merge or resolve conflicting edits with automatic merge, keep-both, or per-side preference
preview syncs, guard against mass deletions, and move deletions to trash
share folders or notes with other people (per manifest)
extras: Not reviewed by Obsidian staff (stated in the manifest). The Google Drive provider is explicitly beta and its sign-in needs a desktop. Users must register their own app with the storage provider. No background service: Obsidian must be running, and on iOS sync happens only while the app is open. Part of a 'Power Plugins' family (Power Assistant, Power Bases, Power Desk, Power Editor, Power Explorer, Power Extract, Power Tables), each sold/working separately.
intentEvidence: No sync subscription, no size tier to outgrow, and no third-party server in the middle.
problem: Obsidian Sync is a paid third-party service, and generic cloud folder tools can silently lose or duplicate edits across devices.

relations.evidence: If you also run Obsidian Sync, iCloud, or OneDrive on the same vault, turn file syncing off in one of them

summary: Vault sync to your own Dropbox, OneDrive, or Google Drive account, with conflict handling, safety guards, and optional end-to-end encryption.
